Environmentally relevant imidacloprid impairs juvenile scallop growth via a dual constraint on energy acquisition and utilization
Post-operative exposure to air pollution and colorectal cancer survival: A multi-center cohort study in southwestern China
Harnessing regioselective aryl migration of pyridone-based aryl-λ3-iodonium salts to access iodine-substituted aryloxypyridines
articles.abstract: Abstract While 2- and 4-aryloxypyridines are ubiquitous in pharmaceutical molecules, efficient synthetic strategies—especially for synthesizing scaffolds with diverse multiple substituents on the pyridine core—remain limited. Here we show a hook-and-slide strategy for constructing these scaffolds, involving the in-situ generation of pyridonyl(aryl)iodonium salts from pyridones and Koser’s reagent (hook, C3 selectivity), followed by an iodine-to-oxygen aryl migration (slide, O selectivity). Such newly designed iodonium salts feature dual vicinal nucleophilic sites, and we demonstrate that using C2 − H imidazolium ionic liquids can exclusively transfer the aryl group to the strategic O site. This approach is transition-metal-free, scalable, and applicable to substrates with diverse electronic and steric properties or complex structures. Importantly, the resulting products retain −I and −NH 2 handles that are amenable to downstream derivatizations, enabling extensive exploration of previously inaccessible chemical space. The utility of this approach is further demonstrated through the concise synthesis of multiple pharmaceutical intermediates and a CRF 1 antagonist, CP-376395.

articles.title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
articles.abstract: Abstract Coexisting populations performing similar functions (i.e., functional redundancy), can stabilize ecosystem outputs under disturbance. The insurance hypothesis proposes that diversity maintains community function under disturbance because functionally redundant taxa differ in their environmental responsiveness. However, how redundancy and insurance interact in microbial communities remains unclear. Here, we examine functional redundancy and insurance potential in soil microbial communities under long-term heat disturbance from an underground coal seam fire in Centralia, Pennsylvania, USA, using seven years of deep metagenome sequencing across heated and reference sites. Functional redundancy increases with disturbance intensity, driven by declines in taxonomic diversity and average genome size and by increased per-genome investment in biogeochemically relevant metabolisms (i.e., carbohydrate and nitrogen). However, a proposed proxy for environmental responsiveness, transcription factor evenness, is reduced in heated soils. These results indicate that prolonged, selective disturbance can enhance redundancy while simultaneously constraining insurance against future stress, shaping microbial community resilience under persistent disturbance.

articles.title: Evolutionary plasticity of bacterial surface layer protein exoskeletons
articles.abstract: Abstract All cellular life possesses environmental interfaces like cell membranes or cell walls, yet the compositional complexity of these major cell components limits structural and evolutionary studies. Prokaryotic surface layer (S-layer) exoskeletons, with their homopolymer paracrystalline architecture, offer a more tractable model of an environmental interface. However, extreme sequence diversity and heterogeneous multidomain organisation of S-layer proteins confound conventional evolutionary analyses. Here, by combining phylogenomics with structural modelling, we show that extensive sequence divergence, modular evolution and lateral gene transfer drive lineage-specific S-layer diversification across both monoderm ( Bacillaceae , Peptostreptococcaceae ) and diderm ( Caulobacteraceae , Deinococcaceae ) bacteria. Focusing on the Gram-positive order Peptostreptococcales , including environmental isolates and clinical pathogens, we uncover multiple S-layer architectures conferring divergent physiological properties. Molecular microbiology reveals that among close relatives utilising the same exoskeleton type, only pathogens display resistance to the antimicrobial immune effectors LL-37 and lysozyme. Furthermore, by experimentally determining two S-layer structures, we unravel how mechanisms including (intra)domain gains and losses generate hyper-diversity of homologous S-layers among clinical isolates of the pathogen Clostridioides difficile . Our findings establish the S-layer as a paradigm of molecular modularity and evolutionary plasticity. Specifically, evolution of a single structural protein enables rapid cell-surface reconfiguration and contributes to immune evasion in bacterial pathogens.

articles.title: Protecting-group-lean platform for synthesizing diverse phenylethanoid glycosides uncovers antifibrotic leads
articles.abstract: Abstract Phenylethanoid glycosides are structurally diverse natural products widely found in traditional medicinal plants and display a broad range of biological activities. However, systematic studies of their functions and structure–activity relationships have been limited by inefficient access to diverse analogs in useful quantities. Here we show a protecting-group-lean synthetic platform that provides a 29-member library of phenylethanoid glycosides with variations at four positions of the central glucose unit. The strategy combines regioselective glycosylation, β-selective glycosylation without neighboring-group assistance, selective caffeoylation, and a mild global deprotection that preserves labile caffeoyl esters. Two glycosylations and two additional transformations can be performed sequentially in one pot, substantially streamlining assembly. Biological evaluation in a TGF-β-induced fibroblast model reveals structure–activity relationships, provides insight into signaling pathways associated with antifibrotic activity, and identifies several compounds as promising leads for further antifibrotic studies.

articles.title: Trypanosomes Maintain Propulsion in Confined Environments by Modulating Rotational Motility from Swimming to Network-Threading Propulsion
articles.abstract: Abstract The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. The mechanism of dissemination within these environments remains largely unresolved, although the trypanosome´s motility is known to play an essential role for its survival. The unicellular flagellate is a versatile microswimmer, like bacteria or sperm cells, albeit structurally more complex than these classical models. Here we study their motility in different viscous and elastic regimes. Using quantitative high speed video microscopy and digital holography microscopy, we detail the three-dimensional mechanical reaction of the flexible cell body with its uniquely attached flagellum to increasing confinement, leading to a network-threading type propulsion. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments.

articles.title: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as saturated bioisosteres of meta-benzene

A defence-in-depth strategy for securing AI-driven biological sequence design
Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
articles.abstract: Abstract Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers’ mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers’ mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

articles.title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation
Interstitial proton buffering enables decoupled transfer dynamics for acidic wastewater decontamination
Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
Chiral SERS and photochemistry via collective hotspot asymmetry in metasurface-templated gold networks with disordered nanoscale porosity
articles.abstract: Abstract Chiral molecules interact with light so weakly that discriminating enantiomers or driving enantioselective chemistry by using optical approaches requires intense circularly polarised lasers or complex resonant structures. Here we combine a geometrically disordered electrodeposited network with a lithographic chiral template resembling the shape of a shuriken. The resulting substrate generates superchiral fields that neither individual component produces. The mechanism underlying this anomalous response arises from two distinct effects: first, the shuriken structures generate substantial intrinsic optical chirality; second, the nanoporous network adds densely distributed plasmonic hotspots and an interference cross-term, which augments the local chirality even more prominently. This chiral plasmonic nanoporous network achieves not only ultrasensitive chiral detection by reaching the attomole range, but also introduces enantiospecific photochemical reactivity on a single substrate under continuous-wave linearly polarised light. Raman asymmetries approach the theoretical maximum ( ≈ 2), while enantiomeric excesses exceed 25%. Finally, a six-order-of-magnitude enhancement over conventional Raman optical activity was calculated.

articles.title: Symmetry-breaking antibody binding reveals extensive capsid malleability in pandemic human norovirus
Structure-guided design of a dual-antigen mRNA vaccine conferring broad protection against Henipaviruses
Impacts of medications for obesity on global health and the environment
articles.abstract: Abstract A new generation of medications for obesity could transform the global food system. While research has explored their health impacts, their implications for global food demand and land use remain unquantified. We apply a global food system model to project the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1) uptake to 2050 among people with obesity under two scenarios: reduced calorie intake while maintaining dietary composition, and reduced calorie intake combined with shifts towards the EAT–Lancet diet. Compared with the Reference scenario, GLP-1-mediated calorie reduction alone results in up to 6.6 million avoided deaths globally in 2050 and 32 Mha more natural land area, reflecting reductions in cropland, pasture and managed forest. Combining GLP-1 use with EAT–Lancet dietary shifts increases these estimates to 7.7 million avoided deaths and 46 Mha more natural land. Lower food prices increase food consumption among untreated populations, including unhealthy foods, partially offsetting these gains.

Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BOx catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
articles.abstract: Abstract The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a Co@BO x inverse catalyst featuring engineered defects localized at face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter. Using an oxidative atmosphere-induced exsolution strategy, we continuously tune the face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase ratio, maximizing the density of stacking faults at a 1:1 phase ratio. Catalytic activity exhibits a strong positive correlation with stacking fault density, with the optimal Co F/H-1.0 @BO x catalyst achieving 32% propane conversion and 83% olefin selectivity at 450 °C—5.1 times that of pristine cobalt boride. Density functional theory reveals that stacking faults modulate Co atomic spacing, weakening the excessively strong BO x -Co interfacial interaction. In situ spectroscopy demonstrates that maximized stacking faults strengthen O-H bonds in surface boron hydroxyl species and optimize radical initiation kinetics. This work establishes subsurface defect engineering as a potential strategy to enhance oxide overlayer reactivity in inverse catalytic systems.

articles.title: Physiological Adaptation of Comammox Nitrospira to Acidic pH Suppresses N2O Production
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas, is a major byproduct of microbial nitrification, yet how environmental pH governs N2O production by complete ammonia oxidizers (comammox) remains poorly understood. We conducted controlled culture experiments with comammox Nitrospira inopinata at pH 6.5, 7.5, and 8.5. Under mild acidification (pH 6.5), nitrification activity was largely maintained, but cellular growth declined sharply, and both N2O yield and extracellular hydroxylamine (NH2OH) accumulation fell substantially relative to neutral conditions. Strikingly, this reduced growth was accompanied by pronounced transcriptional upregulation of core nitrification, stress response, and pH homeostasis genes, whereas carbon fixation genes remained largely unchanged. This decoupling of growth from gene expression indicates that acid-stressed cells reallocate energy away from biosynthesis toward cellular maintenance and proton extrusion, tightening intracellular handling of NH2OH and limiting its extracellular release. Isotopomer analysis (site preference ∼28–36‰) confirmed that NH2OH-driven chemistry remained the dominant N2O source across all pH conditions, and complementary abiotic assays indicated that chemical N2O formation was likely influenced by the diminished NH2OH pool. These results establish that comammox suppresses, rather than enhances, N2O production under mild acidification, opposite to the response reported for canonical ammonia-oxidizing microbes. This distinctive trait carries important implications for predicting nitrification-derived N2O fluxes and refining greenhouse-gas budgets in acidifying ecosystems.

articles.title:
Decoding and Harnessing
Microbial Resilience for Anaerobic
Digestion: Mechanisms, Strategies, and Sustainability under Environmental
Stress
articles.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) is central to the circular bioeconomy, yet its application is limited by the vulnerability of microbial consortia to diverse stressors from endogenous metabolic inhibitors to exogenous contaminants. This Review synthesizes current evidence on microbial resilience mechanisms in AD, distinguishing resistance from perturbation to functional recovery through a sensing-activation-adaptation cascade. The thermodynamic basis of stability is examined through discoveries in direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) and metabolic bifurcation, revealing how syntrophic networks overcome thermodynamic barriers under stress. Multiscale resilience mechanisms are considered from molecular sensors and signal transduction pathways to community-level reorganization associated with functional redundancy and niche differentiation. Bridging microbial ecology with process engineering, resilience-enhancing strategies are evaluated, including quorum sensing manipulation, conductive material amendment, and bioaugmentation with immobilized consortia, strengthening syntrophic networks under internal and external perturbations. A shift from reactive monitoring to proactive management is discussed, using interpretable deep learning models and genome-informed digital twins to predict failures. Critical knowledge gaps include single-cell phenotypic heterogeneity and the synthetic consortium design. Resilient AD systems require a framework integrating techno-economic viability with life cycle assessment, ensuring that they are biologically robust, environmentally sustainable, and economically competitive under variable operating conditions.

articles.title:
Per-
and Polyfluoroalkyl
Substances (PFAS) in Textiles:
Attributing the Fluorine Inventory via Polymer-Specific Analysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in functional textiles for water- and stain resistance, yet their polymer compositions, quantities, and potential environmental release remain poorly resolved by conventional analyses. Here, we analyzed 22 commercial textiles using an integrated approach combining total fluorine (TF) by combustion ion chromatography, targeted PFAS analysis, the total oxidizable precursor (TOP) assay, and pyrolysis–gas chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (Py-GC-HRMS); the latter enabled polymer-specific identification and semiquantitative estimation of fluoropolymer and side-chain fluorinated polymer (SCFP) contributions. Fifteen textiles contained low-to-moderate TF concentrations (0.03–2.57 mg F g–1) and were predominantly associated with SCFPs containing 6:2 and/or 8:2 fluorotelomer moieties, whereas three high-fluorine textiles (143–158 mg F g–1) contained polytetrafluoroethylene together with SCFP-based treatments. Targeted PFAS accounted for ≤0.021% of TF, while TOP-derived PFAS also represented only a small additional fraction, indicating that conventional extractable and oxidizable PFAS measurements captured little of the total fluorine inventory. Simulated laundering, UV exposure, and wet abrasion caused limited TF loss in most textiles but substantial losses in some SCFP-treated materials, indicating treatment-dependent potential for PFAS-associated fluorine release during use and aging. This approach improves polymer-specific characterization of PFAS in textiles and helps assess their potential environmental emissions.

articles.title:
Underappreciated
Role of Free Troposphere–Boundary
Layer Exchange in Ozone Pollution over the North China Plain
articles.abstract: Abstract Ozone pollution control is mainly based on the ozone chemistry sensitivity to precursor emissions. However, despite stringent reductions in precursor emissions, severe summer ozone pollution persistently engulfs the North China Plain (NCP), urgently calling for effective ozone controls. Here, we show that there is strong interfacial ozone exchange between free troposphere (FT) and atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), which renders FT ozone a potential source of surface ozone, but has not been well accounted for in previous ozone controls. We quantify FT-ABL interfacial ozone exchange using an online diagnostic scheme implemented in a coupled meteorology-chemistry model and reveal a significant yet spatially heterogeneous correlation between observed surface ozone and interfacial exchange over the NCP. In high-correlation area, strong downward transport from FT to ABL exceeds chemical production, contributing 52% of afternoon ozone sources under polluted conditions. In low-correlation area, ozone pollution is dominated by chemical production. Derived from these spatially differentiated pollution causes, we propose an expanded ozone pollution formation regime to divide the NCP into exchange-dominated, chemistry-dominated, and mixed conditions. This new regime can better explain observed and modeled spatial differences of ozone trends in response to precursor reductions in 2019–2025. Our results highlight the importance of incorporating FT-ABL interfacial exchange into ozone pollution control frameworks beyond conventional chemistry-based regime.

articles.title:
Mobilization of
Geogenic Contaminants Induced by Seawater
Intrusion in Coastal Aquifers Globally
articles.abstract: Abstract Seawater intrusion deteriorates freshwater quality in coastal aquifers, threatening billions of people worldwide. While its impacts on freshwater scarcity and salinization are well documented, the associated mobilization of geogenic contaminants remains unclear. This study critically reviews the current knowledge on the global distribution, underlying biogeochemical mechanisms, specific triggering scenarios, management implications, and predictive modeling advances of seawater-intrusion-induced contaminant mobilization. A synthesis of 343 studies across 55 countries confirms the widespread occurrence of geogenic contamination in coastal aquifers. Among these, studies from 19 countries (n = 50) document seawater-intrusion-related contaminant mobilization. At the microscale, contaminant release is driven by altered water–rock interactions, disrupted microbial metabolism, and colloidal transport. These biogeochemical shifts are further modulated by specific seawater intrusion scenarios such as groundwater overexploitation, sea-level rise, and tidal oscillation. Of particular concern, conventional strategies for mitigating seawater intrusion may inadvertently alter aquifer hydrochemistry and intensify contaminant release, underscoring the urgent need for optimized synergistic solutions. While some reactive transport models attempt to capture these dynamics, their field-scale accuracy remains constrained by hydrogeological heterogeneities and computational bottlenecks. Addressing these challenges requires multidisciplinary collaboration and high-resolution monitoring of databases. These advances are critical to informing science-driven governance frameworks that ensure the long-term sustainability of coastal groundwater resources.

articles.title:
Internal
Molecular Response Chains to Inhaled Volatile
Organic Compounds for Precision Health Risk Assessment Revealed by
Breathomics
articles.abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are airborne pollutants, yet risk assessment based solely on external concentrations may miss internal molecular effects under low-level mixture exposure. We collected exhaled breath and ambient air samples from 67 child volunteers for VOC profiling, with blood samples from 16 participants used for transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. A physiological compartment-based kinetic model identified 76 endogenous and 44 exogenous VOCs in breath, and dimensionality reduction grouped exogenous VOCs into seven chemically interpretable exposure patterns. These patterns were associated with 86 genes involving cell cycle and neural pathways and nominally with 247 metabolites, suggesting potential variation in energy, lipid and amino acid metabolism, and neurotransmitter homeostasis. Multiomics integration further suggested seven endogenous VOCs as candidate signals reflecting variation across exposure, transcriptome, and metabolome layers. Benzothiazole, 3,7-dimethyl-nonane, and 2-methyl-2-propenoic acid were associated with both conventional cancer risk estimates and cancer pathway activity, whereas conventional cancer risk showed only weak correlation with this internal phenotype. These findings support an internal molecular response framework connecting inhaled VOC exposure to biological effects and highlight the potential of breathomics for precision health risk assessment.

articles.title:
Environmentally
Relevant F-53B Exposure Triggers
Ovarian Cancer Progression via C5aR1-Mediated Noncanonical Signaling:
An Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) Underlying Hybrid EMT and Stemness
articles.abstract: Abstract Significant gaps remain in the health risk assessment methodologies for the PFOS (perfluorooctanesulfonic acid) alternative 6:2 Cl-PFESA (6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate, F-53B), which has been widely recognized as the alternative to PFOS in China. To address this research gap, our study integrated multidimensional techniques to mechanistically construct an Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for F-53B-induced ovarian cancer progression. Our findings demonstrated that exposure to environmentally relevant concentrations of F-53B significantly enhanced the migratory and invasive capabilities of ovarian cancer cells. Within the AOP framework of F-53B-induced hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and enhanced tumor stemness, the upregulation of C5aR1─triggered by ERα acting as a noncanonical receptor of F-53B─constitutes the molecular initiating event (MIE). Following this MIE, the recruitment of β-arrestin1 and Src was induced, leading to the assembly of a C5aR1/β-arrestin1/Src signaling complex. This complex facilitated the binding of β-arrestin1 to β-catenin and drove the nuclear translocation of β-catenin, ultimately activating hybrid EMT and stemness of tumor cells. Administration of the C5aR1 inhibitor PMX205 effectively abrogated subsequent key events (KEs) caused by F-53B exposure. Through in vitro and in vivo validation, our study established an AOP framework that provides a novel perspective for evaluating the potential risk of PFAS substitutes in promoting cancer progression.

articles.title: Physiological and Transcriptomic Responses of Thalassiosira pseudonana to Coated ZnO Nanoparticles and Their Mixtures under Long-Term, Low-Dose Exposure: The Dominant Role of Dissolved Zinc
articles.abstract: Abstract The escalating production of engineered nanomaterials has raised concerns about their environmental impact. However, conventional short-term, high-dose ecotoxicity studies inadequately reflect realistic exposure scenarios. This study evaluated the long-term, low-dose toxicity of bare zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) and four representative silane-modified ZnO-NPs in the marine diatom Thalassiosira pseudonana. Algal cells were exposed for 14 days to individual ZnO-NPs, their binary mixtures (0.001–1 mg/L) or equimolar Zn2+ (0.0008–0.8 mg/L). Physiological and transcriptomic responses showed dose- and time-dependent toxicity, with largely comparable effects across nanoparticle and Zn2+ treatments. Growth inhibition by all zinc forms peaked at 38.0% within 0.01–0.1 mg/L and exceeded 90.0% at 1 mg/L, accompanied by reduced photosynthetic performance, altered chlorophyll a content, and elevated lipid peroxidation. Transcriptomic profiles of all ZnO-NPs resembled those of Zn2+, particularly for photosynthesis- and oxidative stress-related pathways. These similar responses were likely attributable to the substantial dissolution of all nanoparticles and their mixtures (44.3–89.2%), resulting in comparable cellular zinc bioaccumulation and Zn2+-like toxicity. Together, these findings reflect that the tested ZnO-NPs, whether silane-modified or present in mixtures, may behave similarly to dissolved zinc under chronic, environmentally relevant concentrations, highlighting the importance of incorporating such scenarios into ecological risk assessments of soluble metal-based nanomaterials.

articles.title:
Quantifying the
Contribution of Primary, Secondary,
and Tertiary Amines to Nitrogenous Disinfection Byproduct Formation
in Wastewater by Chemical Derivatization
articles.abstract: Abstract Disinfection of wastewater effluent during water reuse produces nitrogenous disinfection byproducts (N-DBPs), many of which are more toxic than regulated DBPs. Despite progress in understanding N-DBP formation pathways from model compounds, the precursors of N-DBPs in authentic wastewater effluent remain largely unknown. Using derivatization reactions adapted from the synthetic organic chemistry literature, this study quantified the contribution of 1°, 2°, and 3° amines to the formation of three commonly studied N-DBP classes in wastewater effluent: N-nitrosamines, nitroalkanes, and haloacetonitriles. Derivatization reactions were first adapted to mild reaction conditions, and then derivatization effectiveness at suppressing N-DBP formation was assessed with known N-DBP precursors. Effluent organic matter was similarly derivatized to selectively block 1°, 1° and 2°, or all amines, and N-DBP formation after disinfection was compared to nonderivatized controls. NDMA formation was primarily attributable to secondary amines; nitromethane formation was attributable to primary amines, with secondary amines sometimes contributing significantly; and haloacetonitrile precursors varied by source, chiefly primary amines in two wastewaters, but secondary amines in another. Irrespective of amine order (1°/2°/3°), amines collectively comprised the majority of the N-DBP precursor pool, suggesting that insights from N-DBP formation mechanism studies using amines as model precursors are likely applicable to real wastewater.

articles.title:
Cord-Blood Metal
Mixtures and Birth Weight: Individual
and Joint Associations in a Large German Cohort
articles.abstract: Abstract Fetal circulating metal profiles may be associated with birth weight, but evidence from direct fetal biomonitoring remains limited. We measured 37 metals in cord whole blood from 1,085 singleton mother–infant pairs in Berlin and evaluated associations with birth weight using regression and mixture approaches. In mutually adjusted multimetal models, cobalt (Co) and strontium (Sr) were positively associated with birth weight, whereas copper (Cu) was inversely associated; none remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Elastic net regression retained no metals when covariates were unpenalized; Co, Sr, and Cu emerged as prominent contributors in exploratory jointly penalized analyses. Quantile g-computation indicated that a simultaneous one-quartile increase in the Co–Cu–Sr mixture was associated with 48.07 g higher birth weight (95% CI: 7.13–89.02 g). Bayesian kernel machine regression and generalized additive models suggested interactions involving Co, with higher Co attenuating the inverse Cu association and strengthening the positive Sr association. Paired maternal and cord-blood measurements showed element-specific differences. These findings suggest associations between fetal metal profiles and birth weight, with exploratory mixture analyses indicating potential joint and interactive associations among Co, Cu, and Sr. Combining direct fetal biomonitoring with mixture analyses may improve assessment of fetal metal burden and health implications.

articles.title:
Continuous and Episodic
Metal Exposures Disrupt Aquatic
Insect Drift, Emergence, and Larval Survival
articles.abstract: Abstract Metal contamination in streams occurs under both chronic and episodic exposures, yet the effects of varying exposure on invertebrate life-history processes are poorly understood. We conducted two 9-day mesocosm experiments with benthic macroinvertebrate communities to compare the effects of continuous and pulsed exposures to dissolved copper and zinc on larval drift, adult emergence, and benthic survival. Our goal was to evaluate how different exposure regimes alter in situ survival relative to the downstream movement of invertebrate prey resources and their dispersal to terrestrial consumers. Both exposure regimes significantly increased total larval drift (29–52% above controls), with Baetidae (Ephemeroptera) and Hydropsychidae (Trichoptera) dominating the drift response. Cumulative daily drift increased rapidly after initial exposure, with Baetidae under continuous exposure showing 3-fold higher drift relative to controls. Total emergence was higher under continuous exposure and was primarily driven by stimulated emergence in Chironomidae (Diptera). Total benthic abundance declined by 24–33% across treatments and was similar between exposure regimes, suggesting responses were more strongly associated with peak concentrations than cumulative dose. Together, our results show that continuous and episodic metal exposures can reduce benthic abundance while simultaneously increasing emigration through drift and emergence, thereby altering critical ecosystem services provided by aquatic insects.

articles.title:
Screening Environmental
Toxicants for Neurodevelopmental
Disorders Using a hPSC-Based Mitochondrial Redox Biosensor
articles.abstract: Abstract Environmental chemical exposure during prenatal development significantly elevates the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), with mitochondrial oxidative stress representing a central convergent mechanism. However, existing screening platforms lack the genetic stability and developmental stage specificity required for systematic identification of neurotoxic hazards across human neural lineage progression. Here, we established a human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-based mitochondrial redox biosensor by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted integration of the genetically encoded H2O2 probe mito-HyPer7 into the AAVS1 safe-harbor locus, ensuring stable expression across pluripotent, neurogenic, and neuronal stages. Using this platform, we screened 76 epidemiologically relevant industrial chemicals and identified reactive oxygen species-inducing toxicants (ROS-ITs) with lineage-stage-selective profiles across neural lineages. Neural progenitor cells (NPCs) exhibited the broadest sensitivity spectrum, revealing neurogenesis as a critical developmental window. Among the screened compounds, bisphenol G (BPG)─an emerging alternative in plastic production─displayed cross-stage toxicity surpassing that of bisphenol A (BPA). In three-dimensional cortical organoids, BPG impaired radial glial cell (RGC) proliferation, triggered precocious neurogenic transition, and induced apoptosis, culminating in disrupted cortical architecture. Mechanistically, BPG aberrantly activated thyroid hormone receptor (TR)-mediated transcription, and the resulting developmental impairment was partially ameliorated by the receptor antagonist NH-3. Collectively, this study presents an integrative framework that unites a genetically stable platform for high-throughput mitochondrial redox screening with organoid-based pathological and mechanistic validation, providing a comprehensive paradigm for identifying and characterizing environmental toxicants that threaten human neurodevelopment.

articles.title:
Can
Small Modular Reactors Enable State-Specific Energy
Portfolios for US AI Ambitions through 2035?
articles.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure in the US is emerging as a major new source of electricity demand, raising concerns about fossil lock-in during accelerated grid expansion. Here, we assess the role of small modular reactors (SMRs) within portfolios that also include on-site solar and wind power, grid electricity, battery storage, and direct air capture. Using a state-resolved scenario analysis for 2028–2035, we compare nuclear-inclusive and non-nuclear portfolios across alternative AI load trajectories, SSP-RCP electricity mixes, and decarbonization constraints. Relative to a grid-only counterfactual, nuclear-inclusive portfolios that achieve carbon neutrality by 2035 require 2.4–47.2 GW of SMR capacity, avoid 0.3–1.3 GtCO2, reduce water consumption by an amount equivalent to the annual use of 28.3–50.5 million people, and deliver \$105.8–194.8 billion in cumulative energy-system cost savings across climate and efficiency pathways. The results show that SMRs can materially expand cost-effective decarbonization options for AI infrastructure, while their contribution depends on timely deployment, permitting, and coordination with state-level electricity planning.

articles.title:
Is Regional Conflict
an Environmental Risk Multiplier
for the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman? Toxicological and Engineering
Considerations

Mind the Leak: Challenges
of Riverbank Filtration
for Highly Mobile Chemical Pollutants
articles.abstract: Abstract Riverbank filtration (RBF) serves as a natural protective barrier for groundwater and drinking water sources. Growing evidence indicates that RBF is minimally effective at removing persistent, mobile, and toxic (PMT) substances, as well as very persistent and very mobile (vPvM) substances, which have recently been established as new hazard classes in the European Union. Owing to their resistance to biodegradation and sorption, these chemicals, including many pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and industrial chemicals, can bypass wastewater treatment and natural riverbank barriers, ultimately contaminating groundwater and abstraction wells for drinking water. Current data gaps as well as analytical challenges hinder identification of PMT/vPvM substances in riverbank filtrate. One major data gap is that many of these substances are transformation products, some of which are formed by riverbank transformation processes. Varying geochemical and transient flow conditions further complicate prediction of the transport and fate of PMT substances, and the evolution of water quality, within RBF systems. To address these challenges, this Perspective proposes a progressive management strategy that integrates source reduction, reactive transport simulations, and nontargeted monitoring, as well as advanced multibarrier treatment, aimed at preventing and mitigating risks from PMT/vPvM substances in RBF systems.

articles.title:
Dust
Storms as Dynamic Multipollutant Exposure Systems:
Environmental Transformation, Toxicological Mechanisms, and Health
Implications
articles.abstract: Abstract Dust particles have long been considered to be naturally derived mineral particles. However, with the increase in regional anthropogenic emissions and atmospheric multipollutant processes, their environmental significance as pollutant carriers and multicomponent exposure media has increasingly attracted attention. Nevertheless, existing studies have primarily focused on dust event characteristics, variations in particulate matter concentrations, or the effects of individual pollutant components, while a systematic understanding of the formation processes and health implications of dust as a dynamic multipollutant exposure system remains limited. This review conceptualizes dust storms as a dynamic multipollutant exposure system and integrates evidence from environmental chemistry, exposure science, toxicology, and epidemiology to discuss the environmental behavior of dust-associated pollutant components, their potential mechanisms of action, and their associations with population health effects. This review aims to advance the understanding of the processes underlying health risks associated with dust storms and provide a scientific basis for the development of future dust-related health risk assessment frameworks.

articles.title:
Cross-Domain
Tracing of Rice Stem Stress under Soil
Cadmium Pollution
articles.abstract: Abstract Plants exposed to heavy-metal-contaminated soil are subjected to pollutant pressure, making timely monitoring of plant condition important for assessing their responses to soil pollution. Although spectral sensing is widely used for nondestructive monitoring of plant stress, the cross-domain association between plant optical signals and Cd-induced physiological responses remains unclear. Here, we integrated spectral sensing with deep learning, Monte Carlo simulation, and omics analysis to systematically explore how spectral signals and physiological responses jointly support the monitoring of Cd-induced stress in rice stems. We found that Cd exposure reorganized interface-associated stress, protective chemistry, and redox regulation into coordinated Defense, Repair, and Adjustment signatures. These biological changes were differentially expressed across the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared spectral regions, producing a reweighting of absorption- and scattering-sensitive information. The agreement between spectral variation and biological stress signatures further established a cross-domain link between stress-state formation and optical detection. Benefiting from this mechanism, we achieved high-accuracy nondestructive detection of rice stem Cd content and noninvasive characterization of Cd-induced responses. A portable spectrometer–smartphone implementation further demonstrated field-oriented feasibility. These findings provide a biological and optical basis for tracking stress progression and supporting timely, feedback-guided crop management.

articles.title:
Air–Water
Interfacial Secondary Hydroxylation
of SO2: An Overlooked and Rapid Pathway to Sulfuric Acid
in Tropical Coastal Industrial Areas
articles.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric sulfuric acid (H2SO4) is a key driver of acid deposition, aerosol growth, and new particle formation. Its formation is initiated by rapid OH addition to SO2 to produce HOSO2, but direct hydroxylation of HOSO2 is kinetically unfavorable. Consequently, the accepted route to H2SO4 proceeds via O2 oxidation of HOSO2 to SO3, followed by hydrolysis. Here, using classical molecular dynamics (MD) and Born–Oppenheimer MD simulations, we identify an alternative interfacial pathway that directly converts HOSO2 and OH into H2SO4. Strong interfacial affinity of both reactants drives this transformation at the air–water interface with a free-energy barrier of only 1.73 kcal·mol–1, substantially lower than that of gas-phase SO3 hydrolysis. Kinetic analysis further indicates that, under conditions of elevated OH, HOSO2, and low SO3, this pathway can outpace gas-phase SO3 hydrolysis by more than 3 orders of magnitude. These results reveal an efficient interfacial source of atmospheric H2SO4, offering a mechanistic basis for its elevated abundance in polluted coastal environments and improving the representation of sulfur oxidation in atmospheric models.

articles.title:
Landfills Act as
Persistent Reservoirs of Rubber-Derived
Chemicals, Driving Widespread Subsurface Migration and Groundwater
Contamination
articles.abstract: Abstract Rubber-derived chemicals (RDCs) are emerging contaminants of concern in various environments, yet their occurrence, migration, and ecological risks in landfill and groundwater remain insufficiently understood. In this study, 35 RDCs were investigated in landfill leachate and groundwater from three municipal landfills, covering raw and treated leachate as well as upstream, on-site, and downstream groundwater across wet and dry seasons. Results showed widespread detection of RDCs in all matrices, with benzothiazoles and other RDCs reaching peak levels of 85890 ng/L, substantially exceeding p-phenylenediamines (PPDs, 869 ng/L) and their quinones (PPD-Qs, 443 ng/L). Although conventional treatment reduced total RDC levels, most compounds remained detectable in effluents (1.10–4946 ng/L). Groundwater analyses revealed clear spatial gradients, with on-site aquifers showing the highest contamination, while downstream groundwater still exhibited significantly elevated concentrations and compositional similarity to landfill leachate, implying subsurface migration. Seasonal variation was observed only in on-site groundwater, indicating that landfill systems amplify climatic effects on contaminant behavior. Risk assessment further indicated that PPD-Qs and 1,3-diphenylguanidine (DPG) were primary contributors to ecological risk in both leachate and groundwater (RQ far above 1). Overall, landfill systems act as persistent sources and subsurface conduits of RDCs, posing long-term risks to surrounding groundwater environments.

articles.title:
Broad Nuclear Receptor-Binding
Activities of Phase
II Sulfate Metabolites Revealed by the Combinatorial Synthesis for
Environmental Research (CoSyER) Approach with Affinity Selection Mass
Spectrometry (ASMS)
articles.abstract: Abstract Biotransformation alters the bioactivity of xenobiotics in humans; however, traditional approaches are infeasible for testing large numbers of metabolites. Herein, we propose a high-throughput combinatorial synthesis for environmental research and a protein affinity selection mass spectrometry approach (CoSyER:ASMS) for assessing the receptor-binding activities of hundreds of metabolites within weeks. As proof of concept, 132 sulfate metabolites were synthesized from 222 ToxCast chemicals using an optimized one-pot combinatorial synthesis approach. Four nuclear receptors (PPARγ, PXR, ERRγ, and FXR) were further selected for AS-MS analysis to evaluate the binding activities of 132 sulfate metabolites and corresponding parent compounds, covering 1056 binary interactions. Interestingly, sulfate metabolites exhibited broad nuclear receptor-binding activities toward PPARγ and PXR, with 29 and 24 ligands detected by AS-MS, respectively. Bioactivities and functional effects of triclosan sulfate and 1-hydroxypyrene sulfate were validated by orthogonal fluorescence assay and human cell receptor assays. Collectively, this study introduces CoSyER:ASMS as a scalable platform integrating high-throughput generation of sulfate metabolites with receptor-binding screening to accelerate the toxicological prioritization of this understudied metabolite class.
